record.paper_title: Slices of Brownian Sheet: New Results, and Open Problems
record.original_question: For a d-dimensional two-parameter Brownian sheet B and each s ≥ 0, let Y_d(s) = {(t_1,t_2) ∈ R_+^2 : B(s,t_1) = B(s,t_2)}. When d ∈ {4,5}, does there exist an event of probability one on which, simultaneously for every s > 0, the set Y_d(s) is finite?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3. Let d ∈ {4 , 5}. Then is it true that outside a single null set, Yd(s) is a finite set for all s > 0?
Open Problem 1 has the following analogue for double-points.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $B = \{B(s,t) : (s,t) \in \mathbb{R}_+^2\}$ be a $d$-dimensional two-parameter Brownian sheet; that is, $B$ is a centered Gaussian process taking values in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose $d$ coordinate processes are independent and each has covariance $\mathrm{Cov}(B_i(s,t), B_i(s',t')) = \min(s,s')\min(t,t')$. For each $s \ge 0$, define the slice double-point set
$$Y_d(s) = \{(t_1, t_2) \in \mathbb{R}_+^2 : B(s, t_1) = B(s, t_2)\}.$$
Suppose $d \in \{4, 5\}$. Determine whether there exists a single event of probability one on which, simultaneously for every $s > 0$, the set $Y_d(s)$ is finite.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches turned up the survey posing this question and related works by Dalang–Mueller (Ann. Probab. 2015) on multiple points of the Brownian sheet in critical dimensions, which address absence of k-multiple points of the full sheet but do not resolve the uniform-in-s finiteness of slice double-point sets Y_d(s) for d ∈ {4,5}. No source verifying a resolution of this specific slice question was found.

status_evidence.title: Slices of Brownian Sheet: New Results, and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Open Problem 3. Let d ∈ {4,5}. Then is it true that outside a single null set, Y_d(s) is a finite set for all s>0?
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Multiple points of the Brownian sheet in critical dimensions
status_evidence.snippet: In the critical cases (k-1)d = 2kN, there are almost surely no k-multiple points.
status_evidence.claim: Related critical-dimension result for the full sheet, not for slice double points uniformly in s.
